item.title: Python library for MarketWatch virtual trading
item.description: I wanted to automate chores in MarketWatch’s virtual stock game (paper trading, not a real broker). marketwatch[1] on PyPI is the small client I shipped — watchlists, game state, portfolio, orders, leaderboard.

item.description: While I was president of AlgoÉTS[1], the club ran its first campus-wide paper-trading competition on MarkÉTS. The numbers below come from the club summary featured on my LinkedIn profile.

item.title: Multiple Technical Indicators Backtesting on Multiple Tickers using Python
item.description: Same BatchBacktesting[1] engine as the earlier indicator experiment, but emphasized at portfolio scale: many tickers, two strategies, equities plus crypto, aggregate winners and losers.

item.title: Experimenting with technical indicators using Python and backtesting
item.description: I batch-ran an EMA crossover strategy across the S&P 500 and a list of crypto pairs with BatchBacktesting[1], using Financial Modeling Prep for equities and Binance for crypto. This post shows what the runner does, how to read the outrageous rows at the top and bottom of the leaderboard, and why none of it is a live trading system. The original article is in French on Medium.
